dedupe_keys.name: seismic fragility and risk assessment of 184 rail and road tunnels in the marmara and aegean regions of turkiye

description: This model by Abdullah Onur Ustaoglu, Berna Unutmaz and Candan Gokceoglu of Cappadocia University and Hacettepe University, published in Scientific Reports in 2025, analyses the seismic fragility of railway and roadway tunnels in the Marmara and Aegean regions of Turkiye, densely populated regions in the active Alpine-Himalayan belt. Coverage: data for 184 tunnels compiled and analysed with three established fragility methodologies; peak ground acceleration at each tunnel's coordinates for a 475-year return period comes from the interactive seismic hazard map of AFAD, the Disaster and Emergency Management Authority; median and dispersion values are chosen by construction type, construction condition and overburden depth. The results were checked against the parameters of the 23 April 2025 Marmara earthquake. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: the abstract was the part read, and the tunnel data are not described as released. The damage state estimates can set tunnel fragility in earthquake hazard exposure and network resilience models for rail and road. It relates to the AFAD earthquake catalogue and the SYNER-G highway and railway fragility curves in the catalogue.
